title: Surprised by Joy
author: C. S. Lewis
place: C. S. Lewis Square, East Belfast
description: Novelist C. S. Lewis on his early life, starting in a big, book-crammed house in East Belfast where he and his brother invented imaginary worlds. C. S. Lewis Square, a plaza nearby, has bronze figures from the Narnia books.

title: Thomas Andrews: Shipbuilder
author: Shan Bullock
description: A short life of Thomas Andrews, the Harland & Wolff designer who went down with the Titanic in 1912, written by novelist Shan Bullock that same year. Andrews worked in the shipyard’s drawing offices. The building is now a hotel.

title: These Days
author: Lucy Caldwell
description: Novelist Lucy Caldwell follows two sisters through the German air raids of spring 1941, the Belfast Blitz. Around 900 people died in one April night, many in the packed streets of North Belfast around York Street.

title: Immortal: The Approved Biography of George Best
author: Duncan Hamilton
description: Sportswriter Duncan Hamilton on footballer George Best, who left the Cregagh housing estate at 15 for Manchester United and became football’s first pop-star celebrity. Drink ended his career early. The city airport now carries his name.

title: The Lonely Passion of Judith Hearne
author: Brian Moore
description: Brian Moore’s first novel: a lonely, devout piano teacher in a shabby boarding house in the streets near Queen’s University, where respectability was everything. Moore left Belfast and never moved back. A fiction pick; the city is its subject.

title: The Star Factory
author: Ciaran Carson
description: Poet Ciaran Carson’s memoir of growing up Irish-speaking off the Falls Road in the 1950s. It wanders from street names to old factories and his postman father’s stories. The title comes from a shirt factory near the family home on Raglan Street.

title: Milkman
author: Anna Burns
description: Anna Burns’s Booker winner: a teenager stalked by a paramilitary in the 1970s, during the Troubles, the 30-year conflict over Northern Ireland’s future. Nothing is named, but it draws on Ardoyne, the north Belfast district where Burns grew up.

title: Say Nothing
author: Patrick Radden Keefe
description: Journalist Patrick Radden Keefe on Jean McConville, a widowed mother of ten taken from her flat by the IRA in 1972 and killed. Her body was found in 2003. Divis Tower is the last surviving block of the Divis Flats estate where she lived.

title: Northern Protestants: An Unsettled People
author: Susan McKay
description: Journalist Susan McKay, herself from a Protestant family, interviews unionists and loyalists about faith, fear and belonging. It is the counterweight to books about the republican side. The Shankill Road is the heart of loyalist West Belfast.

title: Eureka Street
author: Robert McLiam Wilson
description: Novelist Robert McLiam Wilson’s comedy about two friends, one Catholic and one Protestant, in Belfast around the 1994 ceasefires. It is funny until a bomb goes off a few streets from City Hall, the domed civic building at the centre.
